items.stem: A ductile metal specimen is stretched beyond its elastic limit and then unloaded slowly to zero load.
items.workedSolution: (a) maximum force or stress a material can withstand and still return completely to its original length upon unloading. (b) exceeding the elastic limit leaves a permanent extension due to plastic deformation. Core principle: elastic behaviour means complete recovery of original dimensions on removing load.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies key concept: maximum force or stress a material can withstand and still return completely to its original length upon unloading.
Includes exact NCUK precision linked to elastic behaviour means complete recovery of original dimensions on removing load.
States primary causal step: exceeding the elastic limit leaves a permanent extension due to plastic deformation.
Completes full physical linkage without misconception (exceeding the elastic limit leaves a permanent extension due to plastic deformation).

parts.prompt: Define the elastic limit and distinguish it from the limit of proportionality. [2]
parts.expectedAnswer: maximum force or stress a material can withstand and still return completely to its original length upon unloading.
workingSteps: Establish the core NCUK mark point: maximum force or stress a material can withstand and still return completely to its original length upon unloading.
Anchor concept: elastic behaviour means complete recovery of original dimensions on removing load.

parts.prompt: Describe the permanent effect observed after unloading beyond the elastic limit. [2]
parts.expectedAnswer: exceeding the elastic limit leaves a permanent extension due to plastic deformation.
workingSteps: Develop the causal explanation clearly without algebraic shortcuts: exceeding the elastic limit leaves a permanent extension due to plastic deformation.
Avoid the common error of equating the elastic limit with the breaking point where fracture occurs.

items.stem: During a sub-glacial lake borehole survey (exact g = 9.8 N kg⁻¹), a pressure sonde is lowered to depth h = 45 m ± 0.8 m through liquid of density ρ = 1020 kg m⁻³ ± 25 kg m⁻³. What is the absolute uncertainty Δp in the hydrostatic gauge pressure in pascals?
items.workedSolution: Nominal gauge pressure p = ρgh = 4.50 × 10⁵ Pa. Fractional uncertainty Δp/p = Δρ/ρ + Δh/h = 25/1020 + 0.8/45 = 0.0423. Hence Δp = 1.90 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Computes p(Δρ/ρ + Δh/h) to obtain Δp = 1.90 × 10⁴ Pa.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the fractional uncertainties |Δρ/ρ − Δh/h| instead of adding them.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies absolute uncertainties Δρ × g × Δh directly instead of adding fractional uncertainties.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Propagates fractional uncertainties correctly but forgets the factor of g in p = ρgh.

items.stem: On a structural stay-cable testbed, transverse pulse propagation speed is governed by the dimensionally homogeneous relation v = Tᵃ μᵇ (k = 1). A load cell reads T = 320 N ± 2.4 N for a strand rated at μ = 3 g m⁻¹ ± 0.3 g m⁻¹. What is the percentage uncertainty in the wave speed v deduced from dimensional homogeneity?
items.workedSolution: Dimensional homogeneity gives v = T^(1/2) μ^(−1/2). Hence %Δv = ½(%ΔT) + ½(%Δμ) = 0.5(2.4/320 + 0.3/3) × 100% = 5.37%.

markScheme.criterion: Uses exponents |1/2| and |−1/2| to obtain %Δv = 5.37%.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Sums %ΔT + %Δμ without multiplying by the 1/2 power factor from the square-root exponents.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the percentage uncertainties because μ appears in the denominator of √(T/μ).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the combined percentage uncertainty by 2 instead of 1/2 for a square-root power.

items.stem: On a laboratory flywheel test rig, an optical tachometer records rim speed v = 20 m s⁻¹ ± 0.3 m s⁻¹ at radial distance r = 2.5 m ± 0.08 m (where centripetal acceleration is a = v² / r). What is the fractional uncertainty Δa / a in the centripetal acceleration?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2(Δv/v) + (Δr/r) = 0.0620.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the exponent multiplier 2 on Δv/v for the v² term.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts Δr/r from 2(Δv/v) in the quotient v²/r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Confuses percentage uncertainty with dimensionless fractional uncertainty (off by a factor of 100).

items.stem: During a Required Practical wire check, micrometer readings give wire diameter d = 1 mm ± 0.01 mm under suspended tension F = 24 N ± 2 N. What is the tensile stress σ in the wire in pascals?
items.workedSolution: Cross-sectional area A = πd²/4 = π(1 × 10⁻³)² / 4 = 7.85 × 10⁻⁷ m². Tensile stress σ = F / A = 4F / (πd²) = 3.06 × 10⁷ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Uses A = πd²/4 in m² to obtain σ = 3.06 × 10⁷ Pa.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses A = πd² instead of A = πd²/4 (treating diameter d as if it were radius r, off by a factor of 4).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes diameter in millimetres directly without converting d² from mm² to 10⁻⁶ m².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides force by circumference πd instead of cross-sectional area πd²/4.

items.stem: Consider a shipyard dry-dock floodgate sill plate, which has a flat horizontal surface of area 2 m² situated at a depth of 31.5 m beneath the open surface of estuarine seawater of density 1020 kg m⁻³. Take atmospheric pressure at the free surface as 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa and g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the total downward force exerted by the fluid and atmosphere on this surface?
items.workedSolution: Hydrostatic gauge pressure Δp = ρ g h = 1020 × 9.81 × 31.5 = 3.152 × 10⁵ Pa ≈ 3.15 × 10⁵ Pa. Absolute pressure p_abs = p_atm + Δp = 1.01 × 10⁵ + 3.152 × 10⁵ = 4.162 × 10⁵ Pa = 416.2 kPa ≈ 416 kPa. Total force F = p_abs A = 4.162 × 10⁵ × 2 = 8.324 × 10⁵ N ≈ 8.32 × 10⁵ N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 8.32 × 10⁵ N.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes fluid mass instead of total downward force.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses gauge pressure instead of absolute pressure, omitting atmospheric force.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides absolute pressure by area instead of multiplying F = p A.

items.stem: Which description correctly identifies purely scalar physical quantities?
items.workedSolution: A scalar quantity is completely specified by magnitude alone such as mass energy speed or temperature. Verified key statement: scalar quantity is completely specified by magnitude alone such as mass energy speed or temperature.

markScheme.criterion: Selects the accurate qualitative statement identifying that scalar quantity is completely specified by magnitude alone such as mass energy speed or temperature.

options.label: A
options.text: A scalar quantity includes displacement, velocity, force, and linear momentum
options.distractorRationale: Every listed example is a vector possessing spatial direction.

options.label: B
options.text: A scalar quantity is completely specified by magnitude alone such as mass energy speed or temperature

options.label: C
options.text: A scalar quantity includes weight, acceleration, moment, and electric field strength
options.distractorRationale: All four listed quantities are directional vectors.

options.label: D
options.text: A scalar quantity requires a direction angle whenever energy or mass is recorded
options.distractorRationale: Scalars have magnitude only and carry no spatial direction.

items.stem: During quality inspection of a syntactic-foam subsea buoyancy block, a technician measures the cubic specimen to have edge length 3.2 cm ± 0.04 cm and mass 147 g ± 1.5 g. What is the percentage uncertainty in the calculated density of the cube?
items.workedSolution: Since ρ = m L⁻³, Δρ / ρ = Δm / m + 3(ΔL / L) = (1.5/147) + 3(0.04/3.2). Expressing as a percentage gives 4.77%.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Δρ/ρ = Δm/m + 3(ΔL/L) to obtain 4.77%.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds the percentage uncertainty in edge length once instead of multiplying it by the power exponent 3 for L³.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts percentage uncertainties in the quotient m / L³ instead of adding worst-case contributions.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Cubes the percentage uncertainty in L rather than multiplying the fractional uncertainty by 3.

items.stem: Why is the specific latent heat of vaporisation of water substantially larger than its specific latent heat of fusion?
items.workedSolution: Specific latent heat of vaporisation exceeds fusion because intermolecular bonds are completely broken and work is done expanding against atmospheric pressure. Verified key statement: specific latent heat of vaporisation exceeds fusion because intermolecular bonds are completely broken and work is done expanding against atmospheric pressure.

markScheme.criterion: Selects the accurate qualitative statement identifying that specific latent heat of vaporisation exceeds fusion because intermolecular bonds are completely broken and work is done expanding against atmospheric pressure.

options.label: A
options.text: Because boiling raises molecular temperature rapidly whereas melting occurs at constant temperature
options.distractorRationale: Both melting and boiling take place at constant temperature.

options.label: B
options.text: Because specific latent heat of vaporisation exceeds fusion because intermolecular bonds are completely broken and work is done expanding against atmospheric pressure

options.label: C
options.text: Because steam has a much higher density than liquid water requiring extra gravitational work
options.distractorRationale: Steam is far less dense than liquid water, expanding dramatically on vaporisation.

options.label: D
options.text: Because melting breaks covalent bonds inside molecules whereas boiling only warms the container
options.distractorRationale: Neither melting nor boiling breaks intramolecular covalent bonds; intermolecular forces are overcome.

items.stem: A student wants to compress trapped dry air inside a metal syringe so that the compression closely follows Boyle's law. Which experimental condition best ensures an isothermal change?
items.workedSolution: To keep temperature constant, compress slowly inside a thin conducting wall so thermal energy transfers to surroundings keeping temperature constant. Verified key statement: compress slowly inside a thin conducting wall so thermal energy transfers to surroundings keeping temperature constant.

markScheme.criterion: Selects the accurate qualitative statement identifying that compress slowly inside a thin conducting wall so thermal energy transfers to surroundings keeping temperature constant.

options.label: A
options.text: The student should compress rapidly inside thick foam insulation so no heat escapes to the room
options.distractorRationale: Rapid insulated compression is adiabatic and raises the gas temperature.

options.label: B
options.text: The student should heat the syringe continuously while pushing the piston inward quickly
options.distractorRationale: Adding heat raises temperature further and violates Boyle's constant-temperature requirement.

options.label: C
options.text: The student should compress slowly inside a thin conducting wall so thermal energy transfers to surroundings keeping temperature constant

options.label: D
options.text: The student should open the syringe valve slightly so gas leaks out as volume shrinks
options.distractorRationale: Allowing gas to escape violates the fixed-mass requirement of Boyle's law.

items.stem: A battery-electric harbour ferry maintains constant speed 72 km h⁻¹ against hydrodynamic drag of 800 N; its propulsion bus draws 18182 W continuously over 50 s. What is the percentage efficiency of the propulsion drivetrain?
items.workedSolution: At constant velocity, tractive force F = 800 N and v = 72/3.6 = 20 m s⁻¹. Useful power P_out = Fv = 800 × 20 = 16000 W. Efficiency η = (16000/18182) × 100% = 88.0%.

markScheme.criterion: Converts speed to 20 m s⁻¹, computes P_out = Fv = 16000 W, and obtains η = 88.0%.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies drag force in N by speed in km h⁻¹ without dividing speed by 3.6 to obtain watts.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the percentage of electrical power dissipated as heat rather than drivetrain efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides force by velocity (F/v) instead of multiplying P = Fv.

items.stem: From the rim of a deep research shaft, a geophysical probe is ejected vertically upward at +22 m s⁻¹. Take upward to be positive, neglect air resistance, and use g = 9.81 m s⁻² over an elapsed time of 4.2 s. What is the vertical displacement of the object relative to the launch point at t = 4.2 s?
items.workedSolution: With upward positive, u = +22 m s⁻¹ and a = −9.81 m s⁻². Vertical displacement s = ut + ½at² = (22)(4.2) − 0.5(9.81)(4.2)² = 5.88 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses s = ut − ½gt² with g = 9.81 m s⁻² to obtain 5.88 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses +g instead of −g when initial velocity is upward, adding ½gt² to ut.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the factor of 1/2 in the gravitational displacement term −½gt².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the motion as release from rest and omits the upward initial-velocity term ut.

items.stem: During a laboratory dynamics run, a 25 kg low-friction trolley moving at 1 m s⁻¹ is accelerated for 8 s by a cord tension of 50 N held at 36.87° above the horizontal. What is the horizontal speed at the end of the 8 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Horizontal component F_x = 50 cos(36.87°) = 40 N ⇒ a_x = 1.6 m s⁻². Final speed v = u + a_x t = 1 + (1.6)(8) = 13.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds a_x = 1.6 m s⁻² via F cos 36.87° / m and obtains v = 13.8 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses the vertical component F sin θ instead of F cos θ to compute horizontal acceleration.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applies F/m directly without resolving the angled force vector horizontally.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the velocity change Δv = a_x t and forgets to add the initial speed u.

items.stem: Why do commercial PCB designers frequently replace a mix of separate NOT, AND, and OR gates with an all-NAND implementation even when the total gate count increases slightly?
items.workedSolution: Logic ICs typically package four gates of one type per chip, so building circuits from NAND gates alone uses one type of quad integrated circuit reducing cost and unused gates.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that building circuits from NAND gates alone uses one type of quad integrated circuit reducing cost and unused gates.

items.stem: A cylindrical titanium wire wire of diameter 0.500 mm, length 6.00 m, and resistivity 4.20 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m is uniformly redrawn at constant volume so its new diameter is halved (0.250 mm). What is the new electrical resistance of the wire?
items.workedSolution: Initial area A = πd²/4 = 1.963 × 10⁻⁷ m² and R = ρL/A = 12.83 Ω. Scaling diameter by factor k = 0.5 scales area by k² and length by 1/k² at constant volume, so R₂ = R / k⁴ = 205.3 Ω ≈ 205 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Applies constant-volume geometry accurately to obtain 205 Ω.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Only scaled area by k² and forgot that constant volume also changes length by 1/k².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumed resistance varies inversely with diameter rather than diameter to the fourth power.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverted the scaling factor k⁴ when computing the redrawn resistance.

items.stem: A robotic assembly bumper stops and reverses a 0.5 kg shuttle arriving at +30 m s⁻¹ so that it rebounds at 16 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction after 4 ms of contact. What is the signed change in kinetic energy ΔE_k = E_k,f − E_k,i during the impact?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ½m(v² − u²) including negative sign to obtain -161 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes positive energy lost (E_k,i − E_k,f) instead of the signed change E_k,f − E_k,i.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ½m(v − u)² instead of ½mv² − ½mu².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds the two kinetic energies because the velocity reversed sign, forgetting v² is always positive.

items.stem: A high-resistance digital voltmeter connected across an open-circuit lantern battery pack reads 6.00 V. When a 5.00 Ω resistor is connected across the terminals, the voltmeter reading drops to 5.00 V. If the 5.00 Ω resistor is replaced by a 2.00 Ω resistor, what is the new terminal potential difference?
items.workedSolution: Open-circuit reading gives ε = 6.00 V. With R₁ = 5 Ω, I₁ = V₁/R₁ = 1.000 A and r = (ε − V₁)/I₁ = 1.000 Ω. With R₂ = 2 Ω, V₂ = ε R₂ / (R₂ + r) = 4.000 V ≈ 4.00 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds internal resistance r = 1.00 Ω and computes V₂ = 4.00 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumed terminal potential difference stays unchanged when load resistance changes.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculated the lost volts Ir instead of the terminal potential difference IR₂.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Scaled lost volts proportionally to R₂ / R₁ rather than recalculating circuit current I₂.

items.stem: A miniature DC pump connected across a 15.0 V supply draws a constant current of 520 mA for 5 min. How many electrons pass a fixed cross-section of the connecting wire in this time?
items.workedSolution: Convert time t = 5 × 60 = 300 s and current I = 0.5200 A. Total charge Q = It = 156.0 C. Number of electrons N = Q / e = 156.0 C / (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) = 9.750 × 10²⁰ ≈ 9.75 × 10²⁰.

markScheme.criterion: Converts units accurately and obtains 9.75 × 10²⁰.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgot to convert time from minutes to seconds (factor of 60 error).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applied the wrong unit conversion factor for current or time.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplied charge by e instead of dividing Q by e.

items.stem: An engine-valve spring fixture logs an initial collar reading x₁ = 18 mm ± 1 mm and a compressed reading x₂ = 118 mm ± 1 mm under force F = 60 N ± 0.3 N. What is the absolute uncertainty Δk in the spring constant expressed in N m⁻¹?
items.workedSolution: Extension e = (118 − 18) × 10⁻³ = 0.1 m with Δe = 2(1) × 10⁻³ = 0.002 m. Nominal k = 60 / 0.1 = 600 N m⁻¹. Fractional uncertainty Δk/k = 0.3/60 + 0.002/0.1 = 0.0250, so Δk = 15.0 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines Δe = 2Δx with ΔF/F + Δe/e to obtain Δk = 15.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one reading uncertainty Δx instead of 2Δx when evaluating Δ(x₂ − x₁).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts Δx₂ − Δx₁ = 0 on the extension difference, ignoring ruler uncertainty completely.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Leaves k in N mm⁻¹ instead of converting extension from millimetres to metres.

items.stem: On a forestry cableway, an electric capstan consuming 1059 W pulls a timber sled horizontally at steady speed 5 m s⁻¹ for 25 s using a cable of tension 300 N inclined at 53.13° above the path. What is the percentage efficiency of the haulage system?
items.workedSolution: Useful mechanical power P_out = F v cos θ = 300 × 5 × cos(53.13°) = 900 W. Efficiency η = (900 / 1059) × 100% = 85.0%.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates P_out = Fv cos 53.13° = 900 W and obtains η = 85.0%.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses Fv sin θ instead of the component parallel to velocity Fv cos θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses un-resolved product Fv without multiplying by cos θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the percentage of input power wasted rather than the useful efficiency.

items.stem: A rectangular thin-film silicon-carbide bar has length 40 mm, width 1 mm, and thickness 0.4 mm. When current flows parallel to its 40 mm length, its resistance is 2.80 Ω. What is the resistivity of the material?
items.workedSolution: Cross-sectional area perpendicular to current is A = w × h = (1 × 10⁻³ m) × (0.4 × 10⁻³ m) = 4.000 × 10⁻⁷ m², and L = 40 × 10⁻³ m. Using R = ρL/A yields 2.80 × 10⁻⁵ Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses A = w × h in m² and R = ρL/A to obtain 2.80 × 10⁻⁵ Ω m.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Chose the side face (L × w) instead of the end cross-section (w × h).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Converted mm² to m² using 10⁻³ instead of 10⁻⁶.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Rearranged resistivity wrongly as ρ = R L / A.

items.stem: A laboratory kettle element carries the rating "230 V, 1840 W". What steady current does it draw when operated at its rated voltage?
items.workedSolution: Using P = IV gives I = P / V = 1840 / 230 = 8.000 A ≈ 8.00 A.

markScheme.criterion: Applies electrical power rating equations to obtain 8.00 A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divided V by P instead of P by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculated working resistance R = V²/P instead of current I = P/V.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplied power by voltage instead of dividing.

items.stem: During a biomedical materials test, a nickel-titanium alloy wire of gauge length 2.5 m and cross-section 1.5 mm² elongates by 1.875 mm under axial force 225 N, with ±2% stress uncertainty and ±2% strain uncertainty. What is the absolute uncertainty ΔE in the Young modulus in pascals?
items.workedSolution: E = σ / ε = 2.00 × 10¹¹ Pa. Total percentage uncertainty %ΔE = 2% + 2% = 4.00%. Absolute uncertainty ΔE = E × (%ΔE / 100%) = 8.00 × 10⁹ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Computes E and multiplies by (2% + 2%) to obtain ΔE = 8.00 × 10⁹ Pa.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses 10⁻³ m² instead of 10⁻⁶ m² when converting area from mm² to m².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the stress uncertainty and ignores strain uncertainty.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the quantity through an algebraic factor-of-two slip.

items.stem: Why is a fixed resistor routinely wired in series with a light-emitting diode when measuring its forward current–voltage characteristic?
items.workedSolution: Above threshold the LED resistance drops sharply, so a protective series resistor is included to limit current and prevent thermal damage to the junction. Verified key statement: a protective series resistor is included to limit current and prevent thermal damage to the junction.

markScheme.criterion: Selects the accurate qualitative statement identifying that a protective series resistor is included to limit current and prevent thermal damage to the junction.

options.label: A
options.text: In the test circuit, a protective series resistor is included to limit current and prevent thermal damage to the junction

options.label: B
options.text: In the test circuit, a protective series resistor is included to raise the reverse breakdown voltage of the diode
options.distractorRationale: A series resistor does not alter the internal semiconductor junction breakdown rating.

options.label: C
options.text: In the test circuit, a protective series resistor is included to make the diode behave as an ohmic conductor
options.distractorRationale: The diode itself remains non-ohmic; the resistor prevents excessive current above threshold.

options.label: D
options.text: In the test circuit, a protective series resistor is included to prevent the voltmeter from drawing charge
options.distractorRationale: Voltmeter loading is avoided by high voltmeter resistance, not the LED safety resistor.

items.stem: A cylindrical pure zinc wire wire in an electrochemistry cell lead has a free-electron number density of 6.60 × 10²⁸ m⁻³ and carries a steady current of 3.60 A. Given that the mean electron drift speed is 2.78 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹, what is the diameter of the wire?
items.workedSolution: Using I = nAve with e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, the cross-sectional area is A = I / (nve) = 3.600 A / (6.600 × 10²⁸ m⁻³ × 2.780 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) = 1.226 × 10⁻⁶ m². Since A = πd²/4, d = √(4A/π) = 1.250 × 10⁻³ m = 1.25 mm.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly applies I = nAve and A = πd²/4 to obtain 1.25 mm.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reported the wire radius r = √(A/π) instead of the diameter d = 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Used A = πd² rather than A = πd²/4 when solving for diameter.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omitted the factor of π in the circular cross-sectional area.

items.stem: Approaching a toll gantry on a straight test highway, an instrumented freight lorry slows from 108 km h⁻¹ at a steady deceleration rate of 3 m s⁻² for 4 s. What is the speed of the vehicle in m s⁻¹ at the end of the 4 s braking interval?

markScheme.criterion: Converts u to 30 m s⁻¹ and obtains v = 18.0 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts |a|t in m s⁻¹ directly from u in km h⁻¹ without converting units.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds |a|t instead of subtracting |a|t during braking deceleration.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the average velocity ½(u + v) over the interval instead of the final velocity.

items.stem: On an electric kiln element bench, instruments record element resistance R = 10 Ω ± 0.2 Ω and terminal voltage V = 8 V ± 0.3 V. What is the percentage uncertainty in the electrical power dissipated P = V² / R?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2(%ΔV) + (%ΔR) = 9.50%.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the exponent factor 2 on %ΔV for the squared V² term.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts %ΔR from 2(%ΔV) because R is in the denominator.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the percentage uncertainties instead of adding them.

items.stem: A solid billet of machined titanium with mass 1.2 kg and density 4510 kg m⁻³ is drawn without material loss into a uniform cylindrical wire of diameter 1.8 mm (or alternatively melted and cast into a solid cube). What is the side length of the recast solid cube in cm?
items.workedSolution: Volume V = m / ρ = 1.2 / 4510 = 2.661 × 10⁻⁴ m³ (266.1 cm³). Wire cross-sectional area A = π(d/2)² = 2.545 × 10⁻⁶ m² ⇒ L = V / A = 104.6 m ≈ 105 m. Recast cube edge s = ∛V = 6.432 cm ≈ 6.43 cm.

markScheme.criterion: Correct value = 6.43 cm.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Misplaces a decimal factor during m to cm conversion.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides the volume by 3 instead of taking its cube root.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Takes the square root of volume instead of the cube root.

items.stem: Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². A shipyard gantry hoist supplied with 3403 W of electrical power raises a 400 kg marine engine block steadily through 10 m over 16 s. What is the percentage efficiency of the lifting system?
items.workedSolution: Useful gravitational potential energy ΔE_p = mgh = 400 × 9.8 × 10 = 3.92 × 10⁴ J. Input electrical energy E_in = 3403 × 16 = 54448 J. Efficiency η = (ΔE_p / E_in) × 100% = 72.0%.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates mgh / (P_in t) × 100% with g = 9.8 m s⁻² to obtain 72.0%.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits gravitational field strength g when computing gravitational potential energy mgh.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the percentage of input energy wasted rather than the useful efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides useful energy mgh in joules directly by input power P_in in watts without dividing by time t.

items.stem: A rectangular cuboid ingot for a precision metrology reference billet is machined from aerospace al-cu alloy measuring 11 cm × 4.5 cm × 2.5 cm. The alloy is composed of 75% copper (density 8930 kg m⁻³) and 25% aluminium (density 2700 kg m⁻³) by volume. What is the overall density of this alloy in kg m⁻³?
items.workedSolution: Volume V = (11 × 4.5 × 2.5) × 10⁻⁶ = 1.238 × 10⁻⁴ m³. Volume-weighted density ρ = (0.75 × 8930) + (0.25 × 2700) = 7372 kg m⁻³ ≈ 7.37e+3 kg m⁻³. Total mass m = ρ V = 0.9123 kg ≈ 0.912 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 7.37e+3 kg m⁻³.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses an incorrect geometric factor or lever-arm ratio.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps the volume fractions assigned to the two metals.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the harmonic mean formula, which applies to mass fractions rather than volume fractions.

items.stem: On a materials thermal bench, a 605 W heating coil supplies energy for 200 s to a 1.2 kg specimen of water (c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹), elevating its temperature by 18 K. How much thermal energy is lost to the surroundings during the 200 s heating period?
items.workedSolution: Electrical energy supplied E_in = P_in t = 605 × 200 = 121000 J. Thermal energy retained by sample Q = mcΔT = 1.2 × 4200 × 18 = 90720 J. Energy lost to surroundings = E_in − Q = 3.03 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts mcΔT (90720 J) from P_in t (121000 J) to obtain 3.03 × 10⁴ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the thermal energy absorbed by the sample Q = mcΔT rather than the heat lost to the surroundings.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total electrical energy supplied P_in t instead of subtracting mcΔT.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rate of heat loss in watts without multiplying by the heating time t.

items.stem: A uniform block of seasoned oak timber (density 680 kg m⁻³) of mass 10.5 kg floats freely at rest in calm seawater of density 1025 kg m⁻³ (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What percentage of the block's total volume lies submerged below the surface?
items.workedSolution: Floating balance: ρ_fluid V_sub g = ρ_obj V g ⇒ V_sub / V = ρ_obj / ρ_fluid = 680 / 1025 = 0.6634 = 66.34% ≈ 66.3%.

markScheme.criterion: Submerged percentage = 66.3%.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the percentage protruding above the waterline rather than submerged.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses an incorrect geometric factor or lever-arm ratio.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the density ratio ρ_fluid / ρ_obj.
